The page renders its static markup, `blazor` initialises, and\\nthen the runtime dies at startup with:\\n\\n```\\nError: AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage (Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\nhttp://127.0.0.1:5300/_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js)\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js\\n    at un (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    at rn.resolve_or_reject (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    ...\\n    at .../_framework/dotnet.native..wasm:wasm-function[298]\\n```\\n\\nNothing is rendered by any `InteractiveWebAssembly` component; the page sits on its static content.\\n\\n**It is load-dependent, not random.** With one browser at a time it does not occur at all. With eight\\nconcurrent browsers it affects roughly half of page loads.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe runtime starts on every load. Concurrency between independent browser instances should not affect\\nwhether an app boots.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n**Repro: https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro**\\n\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro\\ncd BlazorBootBugRepro \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; ./repro.sh\\n```\\n\\nStock template, stock Chrome, no test framework and no third-party packages. The **only** addition to\\nthe template is a component rendered with `prerender: false`, so the marker it renders can come from\\nnowhere but a started runtime. The repo is the output of:\\n\\n```bash\\ndotnet new blazor -o BootRepro --interactivity WebAssembly --empty\\n```\\n\\n`BootRepro.Client/Booted.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\u003cp\\u003eWASM-BOOTED\\u003c/p\\u003e\\n```\\n\\nappended to `BootRepro/Components/Pages/Home.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\n```\\n\\nThen run N headless Chrome instances at the same URL, each with a fresh profile, and count the DOMs\\nthat do not contain the marker:\\n\\n```bash\\nfor i in $(seq 1 8); do\\n  google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run \\\\\\n    --user-data-dir=\\u0026#34;$(mktemp -d)\\u0026#34; --virtual-time-budget=20000 \\\\\\n    --dump-dom \\u0026#34;http://127.0.0.1:5299/\\u0026#34; \\u0026gt; out-$i.html 2\\u0026gt;/dev/null \\u0026amp;\\ndone\\nwait\\ngrep -L wasm-booted out-*.html      # every file listed never started the runtime\\n```\\n\\n**Measured on the stock template above** (.NET 10.0.111, Chrome 143, Ubuntu 26.04):\\n\\n| concurrency | page loads | never started the runtime |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| **1 at a time** | 8 | **0** |\\n| **8 at a time** | 48 | **25** |\\n\\nThe serial arm is the control: same app, same browser, same budget, same marker — only concurrency\\ndiffers, so this is not the dump being taken too early.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n```\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\n  /_framework/resource-collection..js\\n```\\nsurfaced as `AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage` from `dotnet.runtime..js`. It reaches\\n`console.error` only — it raises no `error` or `unhandledrejection` event, so a page-level error hook\\nsees nothing.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.111\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**ASP.NET Core**: 10.0.11 · **Chrome**: 143.0.7499.109 · **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04 (x64), WSL2 ·\\nno IDE (CLI).\\n\\n**Additional evidence from a private harness, offered because it narrows the mechanism.** The same\\nfailure occurs there, and a Chrome net-log (`--log-net-log`) of a failing browser shows:\\n\\n- **No `URLRequest` is issued for that module on the failing load** — not an error, not a hang: no\\n  request. The bytes never being asked for is the finding, and it is why raising client timeouts\\n  changes nothing.\\n- Across **1,522** `_framework` requests in that browser: **zero** ended with a `net_error` and\\n  **zero** never completed.\\n- When the module *is* requested it is served correctly — `200`, `Content-Type: application/javascript`,\\n  gzip, full length — so this is not the server, the MIME type, or the fingerprint.\\n- A per-load table across three non-victim browsers: **22 of 22** first-of-test loads fetched the\\n  module, no exceptions. A failing load is the one that did not ask for it.\\n\\n**Note on the resource**: `resource-collection.{fingerprint}.js` does not exist on disk; it is\\ngenerated and served by middleware (see #62249). We have not established whether that is relevant.\\n\\n**Why this repo**: the failing import is of a Blazor asset produced by the ASP.NET Core static-asset /\\nimport-map machinery, and the repro is a Blazor template — so `aspnetcore`. The stack, however, is\\ninside `dotnet.runtime.js` and `dotnet.native.wasm`, so if the defect is in the runtime\\u0026#39;s startup\\nimport path this belongs in `dotnet/runtime` and we would expect a transfer rather than a close.\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68697\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Memphizzz\",\"id\":4660924,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Memphizzz\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/4660924?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\"],\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":1},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-21T16:31:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-25T13:23:46Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T21:21:18.169Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7722b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":67980,\"title\":\"Blazor Web: exception during WASM root component activation is silently discarded — InteractiveAuto page stays a dead prerender with no error and no Server fallback\",\"body\":\"### Is there an existing issue for this?\\n\\n- [x] I have searched the existing issues\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\n`WebAssemblyRenderer.OnUpdateRootComponents` fire-and-forgets the root component activation tasks:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/release/10.0/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/src/Rendering/WebAssemblyRenderer.cs#L72-L84\\n\\n```csharp\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Add:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.AddRootComponentAsync(...);\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Update:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.UpdateRootComponentAsync(...);\\n```\\n\\nIf activation throws (component constructor, DI resolution, a type-initializer failure in a dependency that only fails under Mono WASM, …), the fault is completely swallowed:\\n\\n- nothing in the browser console (no unhandled rejection, no `Blazor` error),\\n- no `blazor-error-ui`,\\n- no `ILogger` output,\\n- and for `InteractiveAuto`, **no fallback to Server**, even though the Server registration of the same page works (prerendering proves it).\\n\\nThe user is left on a permanently dead prerender. Worse: once Auto has committed to WebAssembly (runtime cached), even a **full page reload** of the affected page re-attempts WASM activation and dies the same way — there is no user-side recovery short of clearing the cache.\\n\\n**Real-world impact:** we hit this in production when a `TypeInitializationException` was thrown while constructing a ctor-injected DI service during activation of an `InteractiveAuto` page — but any exception thrown during activation triggers it; the specific trigger is irrelevant. Because the fault is discarded, diagnosing the underlying application-side bug took a multi-day investigation across CI bisects and Playwright traces, and ultimately required attaching an `AppDomain.FirstChanceException` handler in the WASM client — that handler is the only place the exception is observable. With ordinary error surfacing, the root cause would have been visible in the first failing run\\u0026#39;s browser console.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nSome combination of:\\n\\n1. The activation fault is logged (console + `ILogger`) and surfaces `blazor-error-ui`, like unhandled exceptions elsewhere in Blazor.\\n2. For `InteractiveAuto`, a failed WebAssembly activation falls back to the Server render mode instead of leaving a dead prerender (the server was able to render the page seconds earlier).\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nMinimal repro (unmodified `dotnet new blazor -int Auto` template plus only the changes listed in its README): https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-wasm-silent-activation\\n\\nA service is registered working on the server and with a throwing factory in the WASM client:\\n\\n```csharp\\n// Client Program.cs — simulates a dependency that only fails on the WASM runtime\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton(_ =\\u0026gt;\\n    throw new InvalidOperationException(\\u0026#34;Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.\\u0026#34;));\\n```\\n\\n1. `dotnet run`, open `/counter` — first interactive visit renders Interactive **Server**.\\n2. Navigate Home ↔ Counter until Counter reports **WebAssembly** (Auto committed to WASM).\\n3. Click the nav link to `/crash` (enhanced navigation), a page that injects the service.\\n4. Observe: page reports `RendererInfo: Static, IsInteractive: false` forever; button does nothing; browser console and server logs are clean. A `FirstChanceException` hook is the only evidence of the `InvalidOperationException`.\\n5. Full reload of `/crash`: same dead result (Auto stays on WASM once cached).\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nOnly observable via `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.FirstChanceException`:\\n`System.InvalidOperationException: Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.302\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n- ASP.NET Core version: 10.0.10 (behavior also reproduced on 10.0.9).\\n- Existing-issue search: `AddRootComponentAsync`, `OnUpdateRootComponents`, \\u0026#34;auto mode fallback\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;interactive auto stuck static\\u0026#34; — closest is #64508 ([Blazor] Unify root components initialization paths), which covers the divergent init paths but not the swallowed activation fault or the missing fallback.\\n- The same silent-discard exists for the `Update` operation.\\n- Happy to contribute a fix if you can indicate the preferred direction (await + log + error UI, vs. propagating the fault to enable Auto fallback).\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67980\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"alexaka1\",\"id\":22166651,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/alexaka1\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/22166651?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T14:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T07:22:48Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

After setting the value to my external identity site ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` (different site entirely), I was presented with ```Sorry, there\\u0026#39;s nothing at this address.``` in the Blazor app. \\n\\nLooking closer at the above line of code, the ```.PathAndQuery``` piece at the end prevents ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` from ever being outside the Blazor app.\\n\\nAs a result, setting ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` to ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` executes a redirect to ```https://localhost:44357/Identity/Account/Register``` (my Blazor app).\\n\\nPlease confirm that this is a bug.\\n\\nEdit: ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteProfilePath``` seems to have the same issue.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/25153\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"hallidev\",\"id\":16142069,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/hallidev\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/16142069?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"affected-most\",\"severity-minor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-auth\",\"triaged\",\"Pillar: Cloud Integration\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":17,\"+1\":9,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":3,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":3,\"eyes\":2},\"created_at\":\"2020-08-22T17:46:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:02:51Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Validate the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` on the request before reading from the form.\\n```\\nThis can be fixed by disabling AntiForgery on the endpoint, but we are not sure if this is correct?\\n- After x amount of time, it seems like the frontend \\u0026#39;forgets\\u0026#39; your authentication. All the [Authorize] attributes return an unauthorized, and getting items from the claims `await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();` returns nothing.\\n\\n**To Reproduce**\\n\\nSteps to reproduce the behavior:\\n\\n1. Adjust the BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto sample to only be InteractiveWebAssembly.\\n2. Deploy the application through: `dotnet publish \\u0026#34;${PROJECT}.csproj\\u0026#34; -c Release -p RuntimeIdentifier=linux-x64`\\n3. Try to authentication/logout endpoint.\\n\\n**Additional context**\\n\\n- DOTNET 10\\n- Template: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/tree/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto\\n\\nIs InteractiveWebAssembly not supported with the sample codes, or there any different changes we need to do?\\n\\n(cc: @guardrex https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/issues/642)\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65368\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Schoof-T\",\"id\":2319986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Schoof-T\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2319986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-auth\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\",\"Needs: Repro\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-02-09T12:00:32Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-19T07:44:43Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. [2026-08-26T21:21:23.322Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7328b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":54365,\"title\":\"Make Blazor WebAssembly work on multithreaded runtime\",\"body\":\"Currently, Blazor WebAssembly\\u0026#39;s internals make use of the historical JS/WASM single-threadedness guarantees as a performance optimization. For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. It\\u0026#39;s OK to have significant behavioral and performance changes when people opt into multithreading, but not when they don\\u0026#39;t.\\n\\n### Approach\\n\\nAs a broad strategy, I think we can:\\n\\n * Factor out some new `WebRenderer` subclass called something like `AsyncWebRenderer` that holds the common logic around serializing renderbatches and accepting the async renderbatch acknowledgements from JS. This can then be used by all of Server, WebView, and multithreaded-WebAssembly.\\n * Use our WebView implementation as the reference for how a complete, async-safe rendering and eventing model should work, because this was more recently implemented than Server and is generally simpler and cleaner. There\\u0026#39;s not a huge amount of code in it, really. If some extra work is needed to queue event notifications, for example, we should see that clearly from the WebView code.\\n\\nI suspect it\\u0026#39;s not necessary to have two different builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly`. The total amount of code that should differ between the threaded and not-threaded won\\u0026#39;t be very much. I expect we can just have two different `Renderer` subclasses and some if/else branches in the JS code.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54365\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"triaged\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-threading\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":26,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":47,\"+1\":30,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":17,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-03-05T10:02:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-21T00:06:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":17730,\"title\":\"Real multithreading in Blazor WebAssembly\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17730\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

When navigating to `/error`, the Error page is rendered statically on the server, then when the client app starts, overwrites the Error page with the NotFound page content on the client. \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe default project should demonstrate how to mix server-rendered and client-rendered content properly in the same app. Currently, the default project itself demonstrates mixing the render modes incorrectly.\\n\\nWhile putting `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` can be considered a workaround, it is undesirable: the layout of the application itself might still be using WebAssembly for even simple interactivity, like collapsing menus. `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting` bypasses starting the WebAssembly runtime altogether.\\n\\nPossible solutions:\\n- Mark server-rendered content to persist on the client after client interactive routing kicks in. Possibly a marker attribute on the element, a directive, or an `@attribute` similar to `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute`.\\n- Allow `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute` to actually initialize the WebAssembly app, but leave the components marked with this attribute as-is in the DOM. Consider renaming the attribute if so. This might be easy to do using similar mechanics as seen in `PersistentState`\\n- Allow customizing the `Router`. For example, allow a behavior that lets the router \\u0026#34;keep\\u0026#34; the content as-is when a navigation event occurs, by overriding/passing `OnNavigatingAsync` or similar, or by inheriting from the built-in `Router`.\\n- Allow supplying a custom `Router` altogether. This would also allow multiple additional scenarios if community-built routers were to show up: handling localization in the URL, multiple hierarchic routers, etc.\\n- Allow rendering content on the server and let the client WebAssembly app \\u0026#34;consume\\u0026#34; the rendered static HTML as interactive. This might be a stretch, but for some simple cases, it can work.\\n- Modify/implement a new `RenderMode` that allows server-client handoff.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n`dotnet new blazor --name BlazorSSRCSR --all-interactive --interactivity WebAssembly`\\n`cd BlazorSSRCSR`\\n`dotnet run`\\n\\nNavigate to the created app\\u0026#39;s `/error` endpoint. The endpoint will show the server side error, then after a short time, the client side router overwrites the content with the client side `NotFound` page content.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.100-rc.1.25451.107\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nThis is NOT the same as similar (possibly slightly related) issues:\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38128\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42561\\n\\nNote that there\\u0026#39;s also the implication that if this is done, \\u0026#34;mixing\\u0026#34; render modes across a hierarchy might become possible. That would also require the user be able to set `RenderMode` to `Static` explicitly, which is currently not possible because it\\u0026#39;s not even defined in `RenderMode`: it\\u0026#39;s condered `Static` rendering when the `RenderMode` evaluates to `null`.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/63842\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"yugabe\",\"id\":14803737,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/yugabe\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14803737?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-09-26T13:34:52Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-02-13T11:20:42Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Navigation.BaseUri;\\n    }\\n```\\n\\nBecause base path defined with slash on the end but current path doesn\\u0026#39;t contains slash the check: `!fromQuery.StartsWith(Navigation.BaseUri)` is true. \\n\\nUnfortunately I cannot define base w/o slash on the end because it breaks navigation.\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/24316\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"michaeldz\",\"id\":1072516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/michaeldz\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1072516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"affected-few\",\"severity-major\",\"Priority:1\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-auth\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2020-07-25T23:02:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-02-05T06:59:09Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

A single app load emits multiple Information-level lines per HTTP request through the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware`, and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticAssets.StaticAssetsInvoker` categories. Because a Blazor WebAssembly boot pulls many assets, this results in hundreds of log lines for a single page load.\\n\\nThe equivalent standalone Blazor WebAssembly app on .NET 10 starts up with only a handful of log lines and stays quiet during normal browsing.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nA freshly created standalone Blazor WebAssembly app should have a console log volume comparable to the .NET 10 experience — roughly: startup banner, listening URL, hosting environment, content root, and not much else during normal dev-time browsing.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n1. Install the .NET 11 Preview 5 SDK (`11.0.100-preview.5.26272.118`).\\n2. `dotnet new blazorwasm -o WasmTest`\\n3. `cd WasmTest`\\n4. `dotnet run`\\n5. Open `http://localhost:/` in a browser.\\n6. Observe the console output.\\n\\nPer-request output (one example request, repeated for every asset):\\n\\n```\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1]\\n      Request starting HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/ - - -\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware[0]\\n      Executing endpoint \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.RouteEndpoint\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticAssets.StaticAssetsInvoker[2]\\n      Sending file. Request path: \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;{**fallback:nonfile}\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;. Physical path: \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;...\\\\obj\\\\Debug\\\\net11.0\\\\compressed\\\\...gz\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware[1]\\n      Executed endpoint \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.RouteEndpoint\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[2]\\n      Request finished HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/ - 200 1376 text/html 302.9165ms\\n```\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNone.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n11.0.100-preview.5.26272.118\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n- OS: Windows 11\\n- Template: `dotnet new blazorwasm` (standalone)\\n- Reproduces with `dotnet run`, `dotnet watch`, and Visual Studio Insiders F5\\n- Same template on .NET 10 (`net10.0`) is significantly quieter\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/66879\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Regression\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-preview7\",\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-05-28T07:11:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T17:50:22Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-07-22T17:50:22Z\",\"closed_by\":\"danroth27\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67048,\"title\":\"Align gateway and templates with Aspire implementation\",\"state\":\"MERGED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67048\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The client-side interactive component starts rendering.\\n2. `AuthenticationState` is requested in the WASM client.\\n3. The authentication state appears to be unavailable or incomplete during this first render.\\n4. Shortly after, the server-rendered state becomes available and everything works correctly.\\n\\nThis only happens on the initial load/hydration. Subsequent navigations behave correctly.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Suspected cause\\n\\nIt looks like the WebAssembly interactive rendering may occur before the serialized authentication state from the server has been fully restored/deserialized.\\n\\nIn other words, the first client render may execute before the authentication payload generated by `AddAuthenticationStateSerialization()` is fully available to `AddAuthenticationStateDeserialization()`.\\n\\nThis creates a transient mismatch where:\\n\\n- SSR has a valid authenticated user\\n- but the first WASM render temporarily sees an anonymous or incomplete state\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Environment\\n\\n- ASP.NET Core / Blazor Web App\\n- .NET 10 preview\\n- Interactive WebAssembly render mode\\n- Authentication state serialization enabled\\n\\n### Server\\n\\n```csharp\\nbuilder.Services.AddRazorComponents()\\n    .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents()\\n    .AddAuthenticationStateSerialization();\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/66644\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"hsolar-hiberuscom\",\"id\":191236407,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/hsolar-hiberuscom\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/191236407?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"area-blazor\"],\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-05-11T12:05:38Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-05-11T13:07:32Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-05-11T13:07:32Z\",\"closed_by\":\"hsolar-hiberuscom\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

I configured the MSAL cache to use localStorage by setting the CacheLocation in MsalProviderOptions like this:\\n\\n```\\nbuilder.Services.AddMsalAuthentication(options =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    options.ProviderOptions.Cache.CacheLocation = \\u0026#34;localStorage\\u0026#34;;\\n    // other config...\\n});\\n```\\n\\nThis works well initially—tokens are stored and retrieved as expected. However, after a few hours (presumably when the token expires), the app doesn\\u0026#39;t seem to automatically acquire a new token. Even when I try to sign out manually using:\\n\\n`await SignOutManager.SetSignOutState();`\\n\\n...any pages decorated with `[Authorize]` still redirect to the NotAuthorized view. The only workaround I’ve found is to manually clear localStorage in the browser, which obviously isn’t ideal.\\n\\nAny insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe expected behavior when using localStorage as the cacheLocation in a Blazor WebAssembly app with MSAL should be:\\n\\n- **Persistent Token Storage**: Tokens (ID, access, and refresh) should persist across browser sessions as long as they are valid and not manually cleared, since localStorage is not cleared on tab or browser close.\\n- **Automatic Silent Token Renewal**: When an access token expires, MSAL should attempt to silently acquire a new token using the refresh token (if available and valid), without requiring user interaction.\\n- **Graceful Sign-Out**: Calling SignOutManager.SetSignOutState() should clear the authentication state and redirect the user appropriately. After sign-out, protected routes decorated with [Authorize] should redirect to the login page or a configured fallback, not remain stuck on a NotAuthorized view.\\n- **No Manual Storage Clearing Required**: Users should not need to manually clear localStorage to resolve expired token issues. The library should handle token lifecycle management internally.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n1. Run a Blazor wasm project with Microsoft.Authentication.WebAssembly.Msal\\n```\\nservices.AddMsalAuthentication(remoteAuthenticationOptions =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    remoteAuthenticationOptions.ProviderOptions.Cache.CacheLocation = \\u0026#34;localStorage\\u0026#34;;\\n    webAssemblyHostBuilder.Configuration.Bind(\\n        \\u0026#34;AzureAd\\u0026#34;,\\n        remoteAuthenticationOptions.ProviderOptions.Authentication\\n    );\\n});\\n```\\n\\n2. appsettings.json with `AzureAd` section:\\n```\\n\\u0026#34;AzureAd\\u0026#34;: {\\n  \\u0026#34;Authority\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;Your-Authority\\u0026#34;,\\n  \\u0026#34;ClientId\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;Your-ClientId\\u0026#34;,\\n  \\u0026#34;ValidateAuthority\\u0026#34;: true\\n}\\n```\\n\\n3. Login into the project and wait until the token is expired.\\n4. Go back to the page and you\\u0026#39;ll not be able to navigate through the page. Token has not been correctly refreshed.\\n\\nNeed to manually clean localStorage to force app to get a new token.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n9.0.204\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/61960\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"galehost\",\"id\":138874295,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/galehost\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/138874295?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"investigate\",\"area-auth\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":2,\"+1\":2,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-05-16T10:10:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-03T12:01:44Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Using local storage to save the tokens and the goal is not to ask user credentials again if the user tries to access the same site till the refresh token expires. This is the time when the refresh token expires(SPA with PKEC in azure B2C has 24 hour expiry for refresh token). After 24 hours the application is trying to login the user through a hidden iframe and for some security reason some of the browsers are throwing a warning and the login process fails.\\n\\nI can see below message in the console\\n`An iframe which has both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin for its sandbox attribute can escape its sandboxing.`\\n\\nI need to know is there any way to fix this. In normal chrome I am not getting this issue, but some other are getting the issue even in non incognito chrome window.\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/510475/b7b4f690-298d-413c-b87e-9c503d3c4a7b)\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/510475/b0eea25b-a532-45c4-8ae3-714b1d0b3751)\\n\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe application should have with some kind of a fallback strategy. Let say if the browser doesn\\u0026#39;t support hidden iframe redirect, then define a fallback mechanism to do a regular browser redirect.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nLogin to Azure B2C \\nUse local storage to store the token cache in client side\\nTry to load the application again after 24 hours(ie after the refresh token expires)\\nSee the browser logs\\n\\n**Note: In case if someone needs to re-create this issue without waiting for 24 hours, then you can replace the access token and refresh token to an already expired value and try this in Chrome Incognito or Mozilla. What I saw is that the url only consisted of `https://xxx.com/authentication/login-callback` resulting in the app being stuck on infinite \\u0026#39;logging-in\\u0026#39;, because with that url the masl.js libarary only returns `operation completed` which is not handled in the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Authentication.RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogInCallback`.\\n\\nI created the following fix by overriding the \\u0026#39;RemoteAuthenticatorView\\u0026#39;, but would like to get your opinion about the possible risks\\\\implications of this and maybe this will need to be fixed in the original \\u0026#39;RemoteAuthenticationView\\u0026#39; aswell.\\n\\n```\\npublic sealed class AuthenticatorViewEx : RemoteAuthenticatorView\\n{\\n    [Inject] internal NavigationManager Navigation { get; set; }\\n    [Inject] internal AuthenticationStateProvider AuthenticationStateProvider { get; set; }\\n\\n    protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync()\\n    {\\n        await base.OnParametersSetAsync();\\n\\n        // Fix stuck in login-callback =\\u0026gt; redirect to home or login\\n        if (Action == RemoteAuthenticationActions.LogInCallback \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; Navigation.Uri.Contains($\\u0026#34;authentication/{RemoteAuthenticationActions.LogInCallback}\\u0026#34;, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))\\n        {\\n            var state = await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();\\n\\n            if (state.User.Identity is { IsAuthenticated: true })\\n            {\\n                Navigation.NavigateTo(Navigation.BaseUri, false, true);\\n            }\\n            else\\n            {\\n                Navigation.NavigateTo($@\\u0026#34;authentication/{RemoteAuthenticationActions.LogIn}\\u0026#34;);\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n6.0(.8)\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43317\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"njannink\",\"id\":3843546,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/njannink\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/3843546?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"Needs: Author Feedback\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"feature-blazor-msal\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 8 Planning\",\"comments\":11,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2022-08-16T13:43:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2022-12-28T18:00:53Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2022-11-10T01:00:55Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Then I try to refresh the page, which includes a component like this:\\n\\n```razor\\n      \\n        \\n          @context.User.UserId()\\n        \\n        \\n            Authorizing\\n        \\n      \\n```\\n### Expected behavior\\nThe page should show \\u0026#34;Authorizing\\u0026#34;, then the code in MSAL that AuthorizeView triggers should automatically initiate a redirect to sign-in, so that the user can go through authentication and thus get a new refresh token and ID token.  (Once signed in, the user should redirect back to the same page, which should show the content within the `` fragment.)\\n\\n### Actual behavior\\nThe page shows \\u0026#34;Authorizing\\u0026#34;, and the HTTP request `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/0c33cce8-883c-4ba5-b615-34a6e2b8ff38/oauth2/v2.0/token`\\nreturns HTTP 400 with \\n```\\n    error \\u0026#34;invalid_grant\\u0026#34;\\n    error_description \\u0026#34;AADSTS700081:  The refresh token has expired due to maximum lifetime. The token was  issued on 2020-11-24T12:56:15.5198672+00:00 and the maximum allowed  lifetime for this application is 1.00:00:00.\\\\r\\\\nTrace ID:  c4360626-5489-4009-89ad-5ae02bd0ca00\\\\r\\\\nCorrelation ID:  228a7671-3752-4ca9-bf1f-7c0c51368fb6\\\\r\\\\nTimestamp:     \\n```\\n\\nThen Blazor allows an exception to be thrown with `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Rendering.WebAssemblyRenderer[100] Unhandled exception rendering component: login_required: AADSTS50058: A silent sign-in request was sent but no user is signed in.` and further detail.  The error is written to the browser console and Blazor shows the standard \\u0026#34;An unhandled error has occurred. Reload\\u0026#34; bottom banner.`\\n\\n### Possible Solution\\nIsn\\u0026#39;t there some way to configure MSAL to initiate the interactive sign-in process on invalid_grant, rather than having it fail fatally?  Or is this just a big bug?  Any such action would have to navigate/redirect or popup on the user\\u0026#39;s browsing page, **not**  naively redirect an XHR request, of course.\\n\\nThis seems to be similar to: https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-js/issues/2219 , though I am not using MSAL.js directly.\\n\\n[This looks like my situation exactly](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/msal-handling-exceptions?tabs=dotnet#msaluirequiredexception), but I don\\u0026#39;t see how I can mitigate. My code never explicitly calls AcquireTokenSilent.\\n\\n### Additional context/ Logs / Screenshots\\nHere\\u0026#39;s the end of the stack trace: https://gist.github.com/szalapski/[REDACTED]\\n\\n(Thought I\\u0026#39;d [post first on MSAL repo](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-dotnet/issues/2248), but they say it is a aspnetcore issue.)\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/28151\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"szalapski\",\"id\":2723505,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/szalapski\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2723505?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"Done\",\"Servicing-consider\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\"],\"assignees\":[\"captainsafia\"],\"milestone\":\"5.0.2\",\"comments\":18,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2020-11-25T17:48:22Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2021-01-13T17:01:27Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2020-12-14T16:52:03Z\",\"closed_by\":\"captainsafia\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *.
